title: Current native peer capability receipt and durable descriptor replacement
scope: Isolated local macOS arm64 actual signed native QUIC peers and public SDK, EdDSA and ES256; controlled Store custody and fresh schema82 boundaries. Server receipt is not publication to other peers, renegotiation or remote consumption.
implementation: Native capability declarations retain exact bounded descriptor and future extensions:16KiB,32 codec/feature entries, JSON depth8,2048 nodes,2048-byte value strings. Full wire scope/operation/expected stream revision, explicit original participant and a defined trigger are required. Empty descriptors/lists can withdraw declared capabilities without changing existing bindings.

New normal communications grants include explicit capability.advertise; existing narrow grants still require that named permission. Store native source checks retain original credential/key, Device, Endpoint, member epoch, generation, live parent and current actor/recipient authority. Service additionally checks the actual original physical binding, controller credential/revision, active media owner and original held source readers.

A claimed offered assurance must agree with the verified current credential; a descriptor cannot create assurance or media authority. Declaration receipt is metadata; no media engine mutation is fabricated.

An opaque attempt captures the exact payload. Descriptor replacement and operation completion commit in one transaction; immutable old replay does not overwrite a newer descriptor. Delayed recording cannot revive retired media. Original readers are released during captured-record storage recovery.

Schema82 registers capability.advertise in native_stream_binding and adds participant/descriptor/trigger checks. Every prior source condition remains byte-identical. Incompatible state is explicitly refused without changing files; no legacy compatibility or downgrade path was added.

CanonicalClient.advertise_native_capabilities validates exact completed Connection generation, unchanged stream revision, participant, descriptor, trigger and stable advertisement record. Legit preparing/failed/unknown outcomes remain visible for original reconciliation. HTTP cannot obtain physical native control authority.
actual_cases: Both algorithms: receive a bounded descriptor, replace it with an empty audio declaration and future protocol/extension values, replay the old operation and observe the newer stored descriptor preserved. Exact descriptor values survive; changing the original trigger conflicts. Actual original audio handles continue carrying marked audio in both directions.

Wrong participant and foreign physical peer are refused, stale stream revision fails, HTTP refuses native control, and a false user-authorized assurance declaration fails without changing the current descriptor.
Actual same-owner current peer can negotiate using connection.offer but cannot advertise without capability.advertise; no operation is admitted and authenticated keepalive remains usable.

A real journal-completion fault leaves preparing with no partially stored descriptor. Audio remains usable; an Identity writer completes after original source readers release. Removing the fault records exactly one original effect and original replay returns completion.
